name: BASS
fuelDetail: PMMA, Cotton, Nomex flat sheets and cylindrical rods
summary: Combustion of flat sheet and cylindrical rod solid material samples in the MSG chamber. Investigation of extinction limits using forced convective airflow and inert gas suppressants.
keyFindings: At airflow below 1 cm/s, the flame is very dim but stable. When airflow increases abruptly, the fire flares up rapidly due to timely replenishment of oxygen.

name: BASS-II
fullName: Burning and Suppression of Solids - II
fuelDetail: Acrylic, Cotton blend, Nomex complex geometries
summary: Over 100 combustion and extinction tests on thick solid materials in forced airflows from 0 to 55 cm/s.
keyFindings: Cabin ventilation velocity (5-20 cm/s) is the decisive factor for flame spread rate in microgravity; eliminates the assumption that fire self-extinguishes in the absence of airflow.

name: FLEX
summary: 284 spherically symmetric fuel droplet combustion tests, measuring the minimum limiting oxygen concentration for flame extinction via CO₂ and Helium dilution.
keyFindings: Helium extinguishes fire through a high thermal conductivity mechanism, while CO₂ extinguishes fire through radiative cooling and atmospheric heat capacity dilution.

name: FLEX-2
summary: Extension of FLEX with interacting droplet arrays and investigation of limiting oxygen index (LOI) at low cabin pressures.
keyFindings: Discovery of the cool flame phenomenon spontaneously continuing after the flame visible to the naked eye has completely extinguished.

name: CFI
summary: Investigation of low-temperature combustion mechanisms (400-600°C) without visible light emission and without soot formation.
keyFindings: Risk of invisible smoldering combustion in enclosed compartments: low-temperature oxidation reactions continue to release CO and toxic substances even when no flame is visible.

name: CFI-G
fullName: Cool Flames Investigation with Gaseous Fuels (ACME)
fuelDetail: Ethylene, Propane diluted with inert gas
summary: Investigation of cool flames with gaseous fuels in the ACME chamber under extremely high oxygen concentration flows (up to 85%).
keyFindings: Identification of boundaries for sustaining low-temperature reactions in rich oxygen environments.

name: ACME BRE
fuelDetail: Flat porous burner simulating evaporating solids
summary: Simulation of vaporization and burning rates of solid materials in quiescent air and very low convective airflow using a flat porous burner.
keyFindings: Materials can still sustain smoldering combustion for tens of minutes in completely quiescent environments if oxygen concentration is high.

name: ACME E-FIELD
summary: Application of high-voltage electric fields to free ions in microgravity flames to partially simulate the effects of gravity.
keyFindings: Electric fields can disperse or extinguish flames remotely, suggesting physical non-chemical fire suppression technology for spacecraft.

name: SAME / SAME-R
fuelDetail: Overheated electrical wire, Teflon insulation, Cotton fabric samples
summary: Measurement of smoke particle size and number density distribution produced from electrical wire overheating incidents and cabin materials in microgravity.
keyFindings: Smoke particles in 0g are significantly smaller (<500 nm) than on Earth due to lack of thermal convective agglomeration; traditional photoelectric smoke detectors are prone to delayed alarms.

name: DAFT / DAFT-2
fullName: Dust and Aerosol Measurement Feasibility Test
fuelDetail: Smoke particles and suspended aerosols in microgravity
summary: Evaluation of the P-Trak ultrafine particle counter (from the SAME experiment) during long-duration operations aboard the ISS.
keyFindings: Ultrafine condensation particle counters can detect fire precursors before they are discernible by the naked eye or standard smoke detectors.

name: Saffire I-III
summary: Full-scale material combustion testing aboard the autonomous Cygnus resupply vehicle after unberthing from the ISS, prior to atmospheric reentry.
keyFindings: Large-scale fires develop heat release rates up to 10 kW; rapid cabin oxygen depletion and CO generation pose a critical life-safety threat.

name: Saffire IV-VI
fullName: Spacecraft Fire Safety IV, V, VI
fuelDetail: Cabin fabrics, Nomex composites, engineering material samples
chamber: Cygnus cargo bay with variable pressure
summary: Combustion testing under exploration atmospheric conditions (reduced pressure, elevated % O₂) and suppression using automated fire extinguishing nozzles.
keyFindings: Confirmed significant increase in flammability in reduced-pressure atmospheres (8.2 psi) even with modest oxygen percentage increases; validated post-suppression smoke filtration systems.

name: LUCI
summary: Sounding rocket flight experiment generating centrifugal acceleration equivalent to lunar gravity (0.16g) for over 25 seconds.
keyFindings: First experimental evidence confirming that weak thermal convection at 0.16g still induces local oxygen supply flows, preventing flame from self-extinguishing as in 0g.

name: FM2
fullName: Fire and Materials in Microgravity (Lunar Mission)
fuelDetail: Next-generation cabin fabrics, Artemis lander electrical insulation
summary: Research project investigating material flammability in lunar base atmospheres (8.2 psi, 34% O₂). Currently preparing for data integration into PSI.
keyFindings: Hypothesizes that the minimum limiting oxygen index (LOI) may fall into the most hazardous regime near lunar gravity levels.

name: SoFIE
fuelDetail: Thick PMMA, multilayer woven fabrics, thin films
summary: Suite of 5 next-generation solid material combustion and extinction experiments on CIR (operational since 2023). Investigating sample thickness, airflow direction, and multilayer materials.
keyFindings: Provides updated benchmark data to replace traditional 1g test standards, establishing baseline data for the Artemis program.
